explanation: Heating ferrous sulphate crystals breaks them down into ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide, turning the green crystals reddish.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Pale green crystals of ferrous sulphate, in a dry test tube held over a flame.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs continuous, strong heating over a flame to proceed at all.

beaker_view.observation: As the green crystals are heated, they turn reddish-brown and give off a sharp, pungent smell of burning sulphur.
